text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet sent a message of condolence to the families of victims killed and wounded by a fragmentation bomb explosion in the central province of Nghe An.

-- A majority of National Assembly deputies, following a stormy debate on draft legislation for coporate tax, suggested that the law should not be applied to foreign-invested enterprises or at least should not be applied to them retroactively.

-- Five banks in Ho Chi Minh City -- Mekong, Dai Nam, Que Do, Nam Do and VP have agreed to form a first-ever aligned bank, with total capital of some $29.7 million. The banks can receive loans from each other at preferential rates and lendings chiefly come from their temporary liquidity.
-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam says it is clear that the Chinese drilling rig Kan Tan III was operating in a Vietnamese part of the South China Sea before being withdrawn on April 2.
-- From 1991 to 1996 the northern province of Lang Son has discovered and disarmed 10,000 mines of different types, liberating 917 hectares of land.
-- The Geography Institute and The National Centre for Natural Science and Technology have proposed a feasibility study for 10,000-tonne ship to dock at Haiphong port.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi visited the military aviation plant A-42, a joint-venture between the Vietnamese, Russian and Ukrainian air forces.
-- A Canadian-Vietnamese enterprise Association has been established in Ho Chi Minh City to improve negotiations between the two countries' governments and enterprises.
-- The Hale-Bopp comet has been sighted recently in Mekong Delta provinces an hour after sunset.
